title: Evaluating shared gene prioritization for type 2 diabetes and FinnGen R10 chronic periodontitis.
byline: Omidi S, Imani SM, Liang G
html:
Objective (s): To assess whether selected genome-wide association studies support shared gene-level prioritization between type 2 diabetes (T2D) and periodontitis.

Design: European DIAMANTE T2D and FinnGen R10 chronic periodontitis summary statistics were analyzed using a custom whole-gene test accounting for linkage disequilibrium, with trait-specific Bonferroni correction. Published Stage III/IV Grade C periodontitis gene results were compared descriptively. Secondary analyses used multi-ancestry DIAMANTE statistics to construct minimum-P window labels, with a relaxed label selected after threshold inspection. Annotation-based elastic-net models were evaluated in repeated nested cross-validation before and after excluding 13 predictors dependent on locus-to-gene scores. Negative matching retained dependence on these scores.

Results: Among 19,280 eligible T2D genes and 19,378 periodontitis genes, 683 T2D genes crossed the corrected threshold (353 using point probabilities and 330 using upper bounds); none crossed for periodontitis. No gene met both cutoffs among 19,275 commonly eligible genes. Three published periodontitis entries crossed the comparison cutoff (0.05/19,496), representing FCER1G and two SIGLEC5 identifiers; none met the primary T2D cutoff. The relaxed window label yielded 50 positive genes, evaluated with 250 matched negatives per panel. Across ten elastic-net configurations, mean pooled area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.527 (range, 0.452-0.583) with full predictors and 0.482 (range, 0.437-0.528) after predictor exclusion; mean pooled average precision was 0.205 and 0.165, respectively. Genome-wide scoring was not performed.

Conclusions: The primary analysis did not establish shared gene-level associations. Secondary models did not justify genome-wide scoring of unlabeled genes. The findings do not exclude shared genetic susceptibility.
